When asked about taking Trump’s name off of the Kennedy Center, 54% of respondents strongly or somewhat approve of it, while 24% disapprove, according to an Economist/YouGov poll from last month.

Meanwhile, a poll from the Pew Research Center in May indicated that only 9% of Americans believe it is acceptable for government buildings to be named after Trump while he is still president.

Trump has since joked that he will look to rebrand an ocean.

results.content:
In the latest Economist/YouGov survey, Trump is exiting August with a 33 percent approval rating, a new low for him in that poll.

Trump’s polling in the Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) average did see a slight increase Thursday, reaching 39.2 percent.

Still, this average marked the second-lowest released by DDHQ since May, when Trump averaged 38 percent. The polling average also found that 57.5 percent disapproved of the president.

A new Economist/YouGov poll released Sept. 22 found Trump's approval rating fell five points in a single week, from 40% to 35%, wiping out five straight weeks of gains in the same poll. The drop leaves him just two points above the lowest rating he's ever recorded in the survey and comes as Republicans enter the final stretch before November's midterm elections. Among Election Day registered voters — those either registered to vote or who say they'll register by Election Day — 49% strongly disapprove of Trump's job performance, and 80% of them say they will definitely vote in November. The same is true of the 19% who strongly approve of Trump: 80% say they'll definitely vote. A slightly smaller 68% of Election Day registered voters who somewhat approve of Trump (who make up 20% of the overall group) say they'll definitely vote.
